title: Isolation and Proteomic Analysis of Plasma-Derived Exosomes in Parkinson’s Disease
author: Wenzheng Hu
materials: The supernatant from step 6 was filtered through a 0.22 μm filter into a 10.4 mL ultracentrifuge tube (Thermo Fisher, catalog #010-1382), balanced with PBS, and then ultracentrifuged using a Beckman Optima XPN-90 ultracentrifuge with a Thermo Scientific TM Fiberlite TM F65L‑6 × 13.5 rotor at 150,000×g for 90 minutes at 4°C to obtain an Exo pellet.
The supernatant was transferred into a new tube and centrifuged at 17,000×g for 90 minutes at 4°C using a refrigerated centrifuge (Thermo Scientific Fresco 21) to obtain a microvesicles (MVs) pellet.

After centrifugation, the supernatant was discarded, unless exosomes (Exo) are required, in which case the supernatant from this step should be collected for subsequent Exo isolation (see the isolation of exosomes from plasma section). The MVs pellet was then resuspended in 500 μL PBS and centrifuged again at 17,000×g for 90 minutes at 4 °C using a refrigerated centrifuge (Thermo Scientific Fresco 21).

Dilute primary antibodies in blocking buffer or TBST as follows: CD9 (Abcam, ab223052) – 1:2000, CD63 (ImmunoWay, YT5525) – 1:2000, CD81 (Biolegend, 349501) – 1:2000, Actinin-4 (Abcam, ab108198) – 1:2000, APOA1 (Abcam, ab52945) – 1:2000. Incubate the membrane with primary antibody solution overnight at 4°C with gentle shaking.
Calibrate the ZetaView PMX 110 (Particle Metrix, Meerbusch, Germany) using 100 nm polystyrene beads (ThermoFisher Scientific) prior to sample analysis.
Use ZetaView software (version 8.02.28) and Microsoft Excel 2013 for data analysis.
Electrophoresis of Equal Protein Mass Samples

The protein concentration of each Extracellular vesicles (EVs) preparation was determined using the micro bicinchoninic acid (BCA) protein assay according to the manufacturer’s instructions (Cat. No. B0010-1, Beyotime).

steps.title: Collect blood sample
steps.instruction: Collect 5 mL of venous blood from each fasting participant in the morning.

steps.title: Initial plasma centrifugation
steps.instruction: Transfer 1 mL of plasma into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 2 500 × g for 15 min to remove dead cells and cell debris.

steps.title: Second plasma spin
steps.instruction: Separate plasma by centrifugation at 2 500 × g for 15 min, carefully avoiding the buffy coat layer.

steps.title: Remove residual debris
steps.instruction: Transfer the plasma supernatant to a new 10 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge again at 2 500 × g for 15 min to eliminate residual cell debris and platelets.

steps.title: Aliquot and store plasma
steps.instruction: Aliquot the resulting plasma into cryovials (1 mL per tube) and store at –80 °C until use.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant and dry tube
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant, then invert the tube on a paper towel for 3–5 min to remove residual liquid.

steps.title: Resuspend microvesicle pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final microvesicle (MV) pellet in 50–100 µL of PBS or RIPA lysis buffer, depending on downstream applications.

steps.title: Resuspend exosome pellet
steps.instruction: Resuspend the exosome (Exo) pellet in 50 µL of PBS or RIPA buffer, depending on downstream applications.

steps.title: Prepare SDS‑PAGE samples
steps.instruction: Denature protein samples as described later, then load onto an 8–16 % gradient SDS‑polyacrylamide gel.

steps.title: Run gradient gel
steps.instruction: Run the gel at constant voltage: 80 V for 10 min (stacking gel), then increase to 120 V for 1 h (separating gel).

steps.title: Activate PVDF membrane
steps.instruction: Activate PVDF membrane in methanol for 15–30 s, then rinse briefly in transfer buffer.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to membrane
steps.instruction: Assemble gel‑against‑membrane sandwich and perform wet transfer at constant current 200 mA for 2 h.

steps.title: Post‑transfer wash
steps.instruction: After transfer, wash the membrane briefly in 1× TBST.

steps.title: Block membrane
steps.instruction: Block with 5 % skimmed milk in 1× TBST at room temperature for 45 min with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate membrane with primary antibody solution (details not provided) as required, then remove the solution.

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash membrane three times with 1× TBST at room temperature, each wash lasting 10 min with shaking.

steps.title: Dilute secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Dilute HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody (anti‑rabbit or anti‑mouse) 1:5000 in 1× TBST.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate membrane with the diluted secondary antibody for 2 h at room temperature with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Wash after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash membrane three times with 1× TBST at room temperature with shaking: first two washes 10 min each, third wash 20 min.

steps.title: Apply ECL substrate
steps.instruction: Drain excess liquid from the membrane (do not let it dry), apply ECL substrate, and incubate for 1–2 min.

steps.title: Capture chemiluminescence image
steps.instruction: Visualize chemiluminescent signals using a gel documentation system (e.g., ChemiDoc) and capture images.

steps.title: Prepare TEM grid
steps.instruction: Drop 5–10 µL of diluted EV sample onto a copper grid coated with Lacey carbon film.

steps.title: Stain TEM grid
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL of 2 % phosphotungstic acid to the grid, incubate 5 min, then carefully remove excess stain and air‑dry the grid completely.

steps.title: Image TEM grid
steps.instruction: Examine the dried grid under a transmission electron microscope (e.g., Tecnai‑G2‑Spirit‑FEI/Quanta) and capture morphological images.

steps.title: Dilute EVs for NTA
steps.instruction: Dilute each EV sample 1000‑fold in sterile 0.22 µm‑filtered PBS (e.g., 2 µL sample into 1998 µL PBS) and mix gently.

steps.title: Set NTA acquisition parameters
steps.instruction: Set pre‑acquisition: temperature 23 °C, sensitivity 70, specificity 70, frame rate 30 fps, shutter speed 100. Measure at 11 positions with 3 cycles per position. Apply post‑acquisition: minimum brightness 25, particle size range 5–1000 nm.

steps.title: Measure protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration of each sample using the BCA method as described in the Western‑blot protein quantification section.

steps.title: Reduce proteins for FASP
steps.instruction: Add DTT to each sample at a 40:1 ratio (final DTT 25 mM), vortex, incubate 37 °C for 1 h in a water bath, then cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Wash samples in TEAB (5‑fold)
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL of 5‑fold diluted TEAB to each ultrafiltration tube, centrifuge at 12 000 rpm (13 400 g) for 10 min, discard flow‑through. Repeat this wash three times.

steps.title: Wash samples in TEAB (2‑fold)
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL of 2‑fold diluted TEAB, centrifuge at 12 000 rpm (13 400 g) for 10 min, discard flow‑through.

steps.title: Alkylate cysteines
steps.instruction: Add iodoacetamide (IAA) to each reduced sample at a solution‑to‑IAA ratio of 20:1 (final IAA 50 mM), vortex, and incubate in the dark at room temperature for 30 min.

steps.title: Digest proteins with trypsin
steps.instruction: Replace the ultrafiltration tube with a fresh collection tube, add trypsin at a protein‑to‑trypsin ratio of 15:1, and incubate at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Freeze‑dry digested peptides
steps.instruction: Place the collected eluent in a rotary vacuum concentrator, vacuum‑dry without heating, then store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Collect peptides (TEAB wash)
steps.instruction: The next day, add 100 µL of 2‑fold diluted TEAB, centrifuge at 12 000 rpm (13 400 g) for 10 min; repeat this wash three times and collect the peptide solution from the bottom of the tube.

steps.title: Activate C18 SPE column
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of 100 % acetonitrile (ACN) onto the C18 solid‑phase extraction column and centrifuge at 3 000 rpm for 2 min.

steps.title: Equilibrate C18 column (step 1)
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of 50 % ACN with 0.1 % formic acid (FA) onto the column and centrifuge at 3 000 rpm for 3 min.

steps.title: Equilibrate C18 column (step 2)
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of 2 % ACN with 0.1 % FA onto the column and centrifuge at 3 000 rpm for 3 min.

steps.title: Load peptide sample
steps.instruction: Redissolve the peptide sample in 50 µL of 0.1 % FA, load onto the column, and centrifuge at 2 700 rpm for 3 min; repeat the loading three times.

steps.title: Desalt SPE column
steps.instruction: Pipette 100 µL of 2 % ACN with 0.1 % FA, centrifuge at 3 000 rpm for 3 min, and repeat this wash twice.

steps.title: Elute peptides from SPE
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 µL of 50 % ACN with 0.1 % FA, collect eluate into an Eppendorf tube, centrifuge at 2 700 rpm for 3 min; repeat once and combine the eluates.

steps.title: Freeze‑dry eluate
steps.instruction: Place the combined eluate in a rotary vacuum concentrator, vacuum‑dry without heating, then store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Redissolve peptides for LC‑MS
steps.instruction: Redissolve the dried peptide fractions in 10 µL of 0.1 % FA solution.

steps.title: Perform LC separation
steps.instruction: Run the peptides on a Vanquish LC system equipped with a nanoViper C18 column (75 µm × 250 mm, 2 µm). Mobile phase A = 0.1 % FA in water; Mobile phase B = 80 % ACN with 0.1 % FA. Apply a linear gradient from 1 % to 35 % B over 90 min at a flow rate of 0.6 µL/min.

steps.title: Prepare MS sample
steps.instruction: Take 20 µg of protein per sample, add the appropriate volume of 5× concentrated buffer to reach a final 1× concentration, then add 1× buffer to equalize volumes. Heat the mixture at 95 °C for 10 min to denature proteins.

steps.title: Flush MS sample chamber
steps.instruction: Flush the sample chamber with sterile PBS filtered through a 0.22 µm filter, ensuring the chamber is completely clean before loading samples.

steps.title: Run DIA mass spectrometry
steps.instruction: Analyze the LC eluate on an Orbitrap Q‑Exactive HF in high‑sensitivity mode. MS1: resolution 120 000, scan range 350–1250 m/z, AGC target 3 × 10⁶, max injection time 50 ms. MS2: resolution 30 000, AGC target 1 × 10⁶, collision energy 25 %/30 %/35 %. Use DIA with 80 scanning windows; total acquisition time 90 min.

steps.title: Import and filter DIA data
steps.instruction: Import DIA data into Spectronaut (v16.0.220606.53000) and retain results with a q‑value < 1.0 %.

steps.title: Set search parameters
steps.instruction: Search against the human UniProt database using trypsin (up to 2 missed cleavages), precursor tolerance ±10 ppm, fragment tolerance ±0.02 Da, fixed carbamidomethylation (C), variable oxidation (M) and N‑terminal acetylation, FDR < 1 % at peptide and protein levels, requiring ≥1 unique peptide.
